scribe.question: Somebody moves the character normalising so it runs first instead of last. What breaks?

options.text: Nothing: normalising early or late comes to the same thing
The footnote markers are normalised away before they can be found
Rules that match on the characters as they came out of the PDF stop matching
The output keeps its ligatures, because normalising happens before the text exists

scribe.question: Somebody makes heading detection stricter so fewer things become headings. Which other rule is most likely to start behaving differently?

options.text: Footnotes, because a note number looks like a heading number
Character normalising, because heading text is normalised separately
Paragraph reflow, because what is no longer a heading joins the prose around it
None: heading detection is decided line by line and touches nothing else

scribe.question: Which piece of information does scribe have while removing page furniture, and no longer have afterwards?

options.text: Which words were hyphenated across a line break
The order the pages came in
Where each line sat on its page
Which characters were ligatures

scribe.question: The output cannot be both faithful to the page and easy to search. Which did scribe choose?

options.text: Easy to search, even where that loses how the page looked
Faithful to the page, even where that makes it awkward to search
Whatever the input already was, unchanged
Faithful for prose and searchable for everything else

scribe.question: A word is split across a line break as `well-` then `being`. What comes out?

options.text: `wellbeing`, because the hyphen was the typesetter's
`well-being`, because the hyphen is part of the word
`well- being`, leaving the break visible
`well-being` only if the word appears elsewhere in the document unbroken

scribe.question: A word is split as `photogram-` then `metric`. What comes out?

options.text: `photogram-metric`, keeping the hyphen
`photogram metric`, as two words
`photogrammetric`, joined with the hyphen dropped
It is left as it was, because the word is not in the exception list

scribe.question: A three-page report has the same line at the top of two of its pages. What happens to it?

options.text: It is kept, because two pages is not a pattern
It is dropped, because two of three is over the threshold
It is kept on the first page and dropped on the second
It is dropped only if a page number appears with it

scribe.question: A line reads `3. We asked each participant to describe what they had understood.` What does scribe make of it?

options.text: A second-level heading, from the numbering
A heading, but only if a blank line follows
Not a heading: it is too long and it ends in a full stop
A numbered list item, rendered as a bullet

scribe.question: Footnote markers used to be found after any full stop. What went wrong?

options.text: A marker at the very end of a paragraph was missed
Two markers next to each other were read as one
Every decimal number in the document became a footnote reference
A page number at the foot of a page was taken for a marker

scribe.question: Page furniture is removed before headings are found. What does that cost?

options.text: Nothing: the two rules do not interact
Page numbers can no longer be used to order the sections
A real heading that happens to repeat is gone before anything can rescue it
The line count per page is wrong by the time headings are found

scribe.question: Two guards stop furniture removal from firing on a short document. One is a minimum number of pages. What is the other?

options.text: A minimum number of words in the repeated line
A minimum number of lines on the page, so that a margin means anything
A maximum number of pages, above which it is assumed to be a book
There is only one guard

scribe.question: You want the running header kept on a one-off letter but still dropped from a report. What is the obstacle?

options.text: By the time anything could tell the two apart, the header has already been removed
Nothing scribe can see distinguishes them: it is handed text and no more
Markdown has no way to mark a line as a page header
The page numbers would have to be kept along with it

tally.question: Somebody moves the sign-flipping step so it runs last instead of first. What breaks?

options.text: Nothing: flipping signs is the same operation whenever it happens
The totals come out positive instead of negative
Every rule that reads an amount has already read it the wrong way round
Refunds stop netting, because a refund is recognised by its sign

tally.question: Somebody makes the transfer rule stricter, so fewer rows count as transfers. Which other rule starts behaving differently?

options.text: Categorisation, because transfers have no category
Rounding, because the totals change
Duplicate removal, because transfers are the rows it is told to leave alone
None: the two are applied to different columns

tally.question: Which piece of information does tally read from the bank's file and then never use again?

options.text: The amount
The posting date, once a transaction date has been found
The merchant description
The account name

tally.question: A summary cannot both match the bank's statement line by line and match what the person remembers doing. Which did tally choose?

options.text: The bank's statement, because that is the authoritative record
What the person remembers, because it is their own statement they are reading
Neither: it reports both dates side by side
The bank's, for dates, and the person's, for categories

tally.question: A transaction is made on the 31st of January and posted on the 2nd of February. Which month is it in?

options.text: February, the month the bank processed it
January, the month it was made
Both, split across the boundary
February, unless the summary for January has already been written

tally.question: The same merchant is charged £11.99 in each of three months. Is it recurring?

options.text: No: three months is not long enough to be sure
No: only a payment with a reference the bank marks as a standing order counts
Yes: same merchant and same amount, in three months
Yes, and it would be recurring at three different amounts too

tally.question: A row's merchant matches both the utilities rule and the fuel rule. What happens?

options.text: It is reported as ambiguous and the run stops
Whichever rule is listed first wins
It goes to the uncategorised bucket, because the answer is unclear
It is counted under both, and the total is adjusted

tally.question: A merchant matches no rule at all. What happens?

options.text: The row is dropped
The run stops and asks
It is counted in a bucket of its own, which appears in the summary
It is guessed at from the amount

tally.question: Transfers are exempted from duplicate removal. What would go wrong without that?

options.text: Every transfer would be counted twice in the spending
The two legs would end up in different months
One leg of each transfer would be dropped, and the money would look like it went somewhere it did not
Transfers would be categorised as spending

tally.question: Rounding happens once, at the total, rather than on each row. What does that cost?

options.text: Nothing: the two come to the same figure
A total that does not add up line by line against a printed statement
Amounts under a penny are lost
The recurring detection stops matching on amount

tally.question: A refund arrives in February for something bought in January. What do the two months show?

options.text: January shows nothing, February shows nothing: they cancel
January shows the purchase reduced by the refund
January shows the purchase, February shows the money coming back
Both show the purchase, and the refund is listed separately

tally.question: You want a refund to reduce the month the purchase was in. What is the obstacle?

options.text: The refund row does not record which purchase it is for
Refunds are recognised by sign, so income would be reduced too
A summary for that month may already have been read, and there is no answer for what happens then
The two months could be in different files
